rv.q: Not only is Dilaria very entertaining, eventually becoming a kind of thriller, but it offers a chance to see three new exciting actors at the start of their careers.
Dilaria is skillfully immoral, a lively dissection of our grotesque attention economy.
As far as satires go, it’s incredibly dark—but also a bit dim.
On page, it is perfect, but onstage, something is missing.
When the character studies are this vivid, and the performances this promising, that’s more than enough reason to go and cheer.

cn.t: Julia Randall's sharp satire skewers social media-obsessed Gen Z with dark wit and pop culture savvy, though critics are divided on whether the staging fully captures the script's provocative energy.
